messages:
maya: Quick flag — p99 for /v1/generate (cohort=mobile) is showing lower than p95 on the dashboard for the past ~45m. EU + US both. looks like p99 ~120ms, p95 ~180ms, wtf :thinking_face:
noah: Do you have the filters applied exactly the same? Could be different sample origins (client vs server) or merged rollups with low counts triggering weird tdigest behavior.
maya: Filtered by cohort=mobile + region=eu-west, same dashboard filter. Screenshot: https://img.prod/snap/… (private)
sam: Another common cause: we accidentally tag some responses as `cache_hit=true` and those short-latency hits get grouped with the same route; if p99 is computed on a small subgroup it can appear lower than p95 of the full group depending on aggregation.
olivia: Good call. Also worth checking whether the dashboard is mixing `quantileApprox` (rollup) vs `quantileExact` (raw). Rollups can under-estimate tails when counts are low.
metrics-bot: FYI — recent note from telemetry: "tdigest rollup merges are known to under-estimate p99 when sample_count < 100" (see #telemetry-notes-2025).
noah: Can someone run a raw histogram / exact quantile over the same window by model_variant + cache_hit? quick CH query (adapt as needed):
```
SELECT
  model_variant,
  cache_hit,
  quantileExact(0.5)(latency_ms) AS p50,
  quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) AS p95,
  quantileExact(0.99)(latency_ms) AS p99,
  count() AS n
FROM prod_requests
WHERE path = '/v1/generate'
  AND cohort = 'mobile'
  AND event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
GROUP BY model_variant, cache_hit
ORDER BY model_variant, cache_hit;
```
maya: ran that for eu-west last hour — results: model-v2 cache_hit=true => n=48 p99=90ms; cache_hit=false => n=420 p99=210ms. The dashboard rollup is showing p99=90ms at the endpoint level, p95=180ms. So dashboard p99 is picking the small cache_hit subgroup's p99 somehow.
sam: ahh that confirms mixing. If the dashboard rollup merges variant-level tdigests with different weights and then we display a route-level quantile without proper weighting it can pick the wrong slice. We need to ensure rollups preserve sample_count and compute weighted quantiles, or show an explicit sample_count warning.
noah: UX proposal: on the p50/p95/p99 tiles show a small sample-count badge and a tooltip: "p99 computed from rollup t-digests; low sample counts (<100) can under-estimate tails — click to see raw histogram". Also add a small yellow warning icon when counts differ across variants by >10x.
olivia: Ops action: we should fix two things: 1) fix rollup merge to use weighted quantiles (or fallback to raw histogram for p99 when global sample_count < threshold), 2) improve console UI to surface sample counts + origin of sample (client vs server vs cached). I'll open an RFC draft.
sam: short-term mitigation: change the dashboard to compute p99 from raw events for the last 15m window for endpoint-level views (costly but limited window). Long term: update rollup contract.
metrics-bot: Logged an internal ticket: METRICS-8421 — "Route-level p99 under-estimation due to tdigest merge and cache_hit skew".
deploy-bot: @olivia set to assigned, priority=P2.
maya: Thanks all. Can we also add an affordance in the rollout page where we compare baseline vs canary that says if p99s are based on rollups w/ low counts, mark as "unstable"? saw a near-miss earlier.
noah: Agree. I'll add a checklist item for rollout gating: require either raw-sample p99 or min-sample-count for rollup p99 to be used in decisions.
maya: Action items: olivia — RFC + ticket, sam — short-term raw-15m fallback change, noah — rollout gating checklist PR, I'll monitor the dashboard and follow up tomorrow morning. :thumbsup: :eyes:
olivia: I'll start the RFC now, cc @metrics-bot for notes.
metrics-bot: Noted. Arch note: we may also want to include `cache_hit` as a default breakdown in endpoint views to make this class of issue more discoverable.
noah: one more: add a small explain snippet in the console docs about "why p99 < p95 sometimes" — short paragraph and link to METRICS-8421.
maya: perfect. Thanks team.
